title: Japan 5-Year Climate Transition Bond (GX) auction (~¥250bn anticipated) — the other 5-year supply event in the BoJ's deepest-tapered bucket, ten days before the regular 5-year
source: EST: mof.go.jp English November 2026 auction calendar (english/policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2611e.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 25,187 bytes) by the jgb-5y-auction-2026-11-12 initial research; parsed cell by cell, its first table row reads 'Nov. 2, 2026 | 5-year Japan Climate Transition Bonds'. The row carries no issue number and no 'Auction Announcement' href on 2026-09-09, so the auction has not been announced and NO SIZE IS ASSERTED. ~¥250bn is the anticipated base case from MOF's own Auction Results for JGBs workbook (english/policy/jgbs/auction/past_auction_results/Auction_Results_for_JGBs.xls, 492,032 bytes, last saved 2026-08-13, parsed 2026-09-09), whose GX5年債 sheet carries the entire history of this instrument in six rows — issue 1 at ¥800bn (2024-02-27), issue 2 at ¥350bn twice (2024-07-18, 2025-01-29), issue 3 at ¥300bn (2025-07-15), issue 4 at ¥300bn (2026-01-26) and issue 5 at ¥250bn (2026-05-25) — a monotone decline after the inaugural print, with the two most recent 2026 auctions on the calendar's own rows (Jan. 26 and May 25, both carrying announcement hrefs and issue numbers) confirming a roughly twice-to-three-times-a-year cadence rather than a monthly one. Filed `estimate` on the same three counts every JGB entry on this calendar records and one more: the size is anticipated rather than announced, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the cadence is too irregular (roughly 2-3 a year, no fixed weekday or week-of-month) for the date to be reproduced from arithmetic the way the regular monthly auctions can be. The DATE is MOF's own and is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy and the size, not about the evidence
notes: Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of jgb-5y-auction-2026-11-12, on MOF's own November calendar. It sits D-10 from the proposing event — outside the ±5-day corridor, and proposed on evidence rather than on proximity, the same basis the proposing event was itself filed on. THE MEASURED REASON IT IS WORTH TRACKING: it is the only other event on this calendar that puts Japanese government paper into the BoJ's 3-5y purchase bucket, the bucket the proposing ledger measured at −62.3% (¥1,701.4bn/month in 2024-01 → ¥641.0bn in 2026-08, read from 32 BoJ monthly operation workbooks ope2401→ope2608, all HTTP 200). That bucket's net supply to private hands rose +132.8% over the window, and the ~¥250bn anticipated here is roughly 10% of the regular 5-year's ¥2,500bn — small, but it lands ten days ahead of it and inside the same absorption problem. It also gives the 5-year sector a second, differently-structured demand read: across the six auctions of its five issues since 2024-02 the GX 5-year has covered 3.19x to 4.62x on offerings a fraction the regular auction's size, so a weak GX print alongside a normal regular print (or the reverse) separates 'the 5-year sector is fine' from 'the regular 5-year's bid is fine'. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is low for the reasons every sibling JGB ledger records: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and no house playbook is rates-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
